title: Career Roadmap: Cyber Forensics Analyst
summary: A Cyber Forensics Analyst investigates digital devices, systems, and data to determine what happened during a suspected cyber incident or digital crime. The role involves collecting and examining digital evidence, reconstructing events, identifying suspicious activity, and preparing reports that can support internal investigations or legal proceedings.

blocks.text: A Cyber Forensics Analyst investigates digital devices, systems, and data to determine what happened during a suspected cyber incident or digital crime. The role involves collecting and examining digital evidence, reconstructing events, identifying suspicious activity, and preparing reports that can support internal investigations or legal proceedings.
A B.Sc in Cyber Security or Digital Forensics provides a relevant foundation in operating systems, computer networks, cybersecurity, evidence handling, and investigative methods.

blocks.label: Computer Forensics Analyst
blocks.text: Examines computers, storage devices, files, and operating-system artefacts.

blocks.label: Mobile Device Forensics Analyst
blocks.text: Investigates supported mobile-device data and application artefacts.

blocks.label: Network Forensics Analyst
blocks.text: Analyses network traffic and connection records to reconstruct suspicious activity.

blocks.label: Incident Response Analyst
blocks.text: Investigates security incidents and supports containment and recovery.

blocks.label: Digital Evidence Examiner
blocks.text: Processes and documents evidence for corporate, government, or legal investigations.

sections.heading: What does a Cyber Forensics Analyst do?

items.text: Receive investigation requests and establish the scope of an examination.
Preserve digital evidence and document its collection and handling.
Create forensic copies or images of supported storage media using approved procedures.
Calculate and verify cryptographic hashes to help establish evidence integrity.
Examine file-system artefacts, logs, metadata, browser activity, and relevant timelines.
Investigate suspicious files, account activity, and indicators of compromise.
Correlate findings across devices, applications, networks, and security logs.
Document methodology, findings, limitations, and supporting evidence.
Prepare clear technical reports for investigators, security teams, legal professionals, or authorised decision-makers.
